paper_metadata.title: Influence of Mo and Ru additions on the creep behavior of Ni-based single crystal superalloys at 1100 °C

evidence.quote: the role of Ru playing in the microstructure and creep performance at 1100 °C and 140 MPa was evaluated in this study

Seven alloys in a series of Ni-based single crystal superalloys with diﬀerent Co (~ 7.0 and 15.0 wt%), Cr (~ 3.5 and 6.0 wt%), Mo (~ 1.0 and 2.5 wt%) and Ru (~ 2.5 and 4.0 wt%) additions were examined in this study.

Single crystal bars with the growth orientation < 001 > (15 mm in diameter and 150 mm in length) were directionally solidiﬁed at the Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials.

Standard heat treatment (solution treatment at elevated temperature in the range of 1300 –1335 °C for 8– 16 h followed by the two-stage aging at 1150 °C for 4 h and 870 °C for 24 h) was performed on the directionally solidiﬁed single crystal bars.

Mo with a large diﬀerence in the electronic structure and atomic radius from Ni is added into Ni-based single crystal superalloys for its signiﬁcant solid solution strengthening in the γ matrix [1].

The high temperature and low stress creep performance could be enhanced by the co-addition of Mo and Ru since their synergistic eﬀect could be able to enhance the γ/γ' interfacial strengthening and retain the mi- crostructural stability.
